claims.text: Integrating cryogenic cooling into additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi powder will reduce residual thermal stresses relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
Cryogenic-assisted processing will reduce degradation of the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi components.
The initial AlCrFeNiSi feedstock is as-atomized powder with a typical particle-size distribution.
The initial AlCrFeNiSi powder has inherent surface oxide levels.
A cryogenic medium such as a liquid-nitrogen-cooled system can maintain a low build-platform temperature during processing.
Cryogenic cooling will lower thermal gradients during selective laser melting.
Lower thermal gradients will reduce the development of residual thermal stresses.
Cryogenic-assisted processing will suppress excessive grain coarsening.
The cryogenic environment will rapidly extract heat from the molten pool.
Rapid extraction of heat from the molten pool will minimize thermal gradients.
Cryogenic heat extraction will produce quenching-induced microstructure stabilization.
Cryogenic-assisted processing will produce more homogeneous microstructural features.
Lower residual stress and greater microstructural homogeneity will enhance mechanical performance.
Cryogenic-assisted processing will reduce processing complexity by reducing the need for post-build corrective treatments.
Cryogenically processed miniature components will have higher tensile strength than conventionally processed controls.
Cryogenically processed miniature components will have higher hardness than conventionally processed controls.
Cryogenically processed miniature components will have higher ductility than conventionally processed controls.
The effectiveness of cryogenic cooling will be most pronounced for components with characteristic dimensions below 10 mm.
Scaling the cryogenic-assisted process to larger components may present integration challenges.
No direct empirical evidence is provided for cryogenic additive manufacturing of this AlCrFeNiSi system.
